mainTopic: הסתר פנים, God's crying over the חורבן, stories about honoring Torah and its scholars, and a return to the משנה's definition of a קטן
overview: The amud opens as רבא finishes his rule that whoever never suffers הסתר פנים is not one of the Jewish people. The רבנן say רבא himself seems free of trouble, he answers that he secretly pays the Persian king, and after they keep looking at him with suspicion he is arrested. רבא and רב יוסף then teach that even when God hides His face, He still speaks to us in dreams and protects us with His hand. Stories about רבי יהושע בן חנניה follow: he beats a heretic in a silent sign debate before the Caesar, and on his deathbed he comforts the רבנן that the nations' wisdom falls together with Israel's. Next come teachings about God reviewing a person's speech at death, and about God crying in a hidden place over the חורבן and the exile, with רבי dropping the book of איכה in grief. Two stories then show the value of Torah scholars and Torah learning: a blind scholar blesses רבי and רבי חייא for greeting him, and רבי יוחנן defends רב אידי by teaching that one day of Torah a year counts as a whole year. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's definition of a קטן, and רבי זירא begins a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבא's rule about who belongs to the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: The last words of רבא's rule: whoever is not under הסתר פנים and 'והיה לאכול' is not one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...is not from among them.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a rule רבא stated just before this section. Anyone who never feels God hiding His face, and is never 'devoured' by enemies, is not truly one of the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule sounds harsh, but it treats suffering under הסתר פנים as a sign that someone belongs to the people the פסוק speaks about. This rule sets up the next step, where the רבנן turn it back on רבא himself.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not from among them
God 'hiding His face', meaning He seems distant

phrases.english: is not from among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever does not suffer הסתר פנים and 'והיה לאכול' is not one of the Jewish people.

steps.title: The Sages point out that רבא himself seems free of these troubles
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבא that he does not seem to suffer הסתר פנים or 'והיה לאכול', so by his own rule he would not be one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to רבא: Master, you are not under the hiding of the face, and you are not under 'and they shall be devoured'!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבא with his own rule. His prayers seem to be answered and the government doesn't take his money, so where is his suffering?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is true, רבא would have to count himself outside the people, which makes no sense. The challenge forces רבא to show that he does suffer in some hidden way.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way to address a rabbi
'And they shall be devoured', the second curse in the פסוק

phrases.english: The Sages said to Rava:
Master, you are not under the hiding of the face,
and you are not under 'and they shall be devoured'!
phrases.notes: דברים 31:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's rule against him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא seems free of both troubles, so by his own rule he would not be one of the people.

steps.title: רבא reveals he secretly pays the king
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he secretly sends many payments to King שבור's house, so he is in fact being 'devoured'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do you know how much I send in secret to the house of King שבור?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He says he is suffering too, just quietly: he has to send a lot of money in secret to the Persian king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His good situation is only how things look from outside. The hidden payments count as 'being devoured', so he still fits inside his own rule.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Do you know how much I send
in secret to the house of King Shapur?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא secretly pays heavily to the king, so he is 'devoured' too.

steps.title: The Sages look at רבא and he is arrested
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן still look at רבא with suspicion, and right then King שבור's men come and arrest him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the רבנן set their eyes upon him. Meanwhile, the house of King שבור sent for him and they seized him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells what happened next. The רבנן were not convinced and kept looking at him, and soon the king's people arrested him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story suggests the רבנן's gaze had a real effect: right after it, trouble came upon רבא. This sets up the next step, where רבא connects it to a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: They set their eyes on him, looked at him with suspicion

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, יְהַבוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן עֵינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Even so, the Sages set their eyes upon him.
Meanwhile, the house of King Shapur sent for him
and they seized him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי יְהַבוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן עֵינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the רבנן looked at him, רבא was arrested.

steps.title: רבא links his arrest to a teaching of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא says this matches the ברייתא: wherever חכמים set their eyes, the result is death or poverty.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: This is what is taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: Wherever the חכמים set their eyes, there is either death or poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains his own arrest using a ברייתא. When חכמים look at someone this way, death or poverty follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story gets a source: the gaze of חכמים has real power. רבא's arrest, which cost him money, is the 'poverty' side of that teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is taught in a ברייתא
The Sages set their eyes (on someone)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן doubted רבא's answer, he was arrested, and he saw it as the ברייתא coming true: the gaze of חכמים brings death or poverty.

phrases.english: He said: This is what is taught:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Wherever 'the Sages set their eyes' —
there is either death or poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the arrest with a ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The gaze of חכמים brings death or poverty, as happened to רבא.

steps.title: רבא: even when God hides His face, He speaks in dreams
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'ואנכי הסתר אסתיר פני', רבא says that even during the hiding, God still speaks to us through dreams.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And I will surely hide My face on that day.' רבא said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Even though I hid My face from them, 'I speak with him in a dream.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new idea about הסתר פנים. רבא says God has not cut us off completely, because He still talks to us in dreams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא softens the harsh meaning of הסתר פנים. The open connection is hidden, but a quieter one through dreams remains.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
I speak with him in a dream

phrases.english: 'And I will surely hide My face on that day,'
phrases.notes: דברים 31:18

phrases.english: Rava said,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִסְתַּרְתִּי פָּנַי מֵהֶם —
phrases.english: Even though I hid My face from them —
'I speak with him in a dream.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:6

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָנֹכִי הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר פָּנַי בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new explanation of the הסתר פנים פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even during הסתר פנים, God speaks to us in dreams.

steps.title: רב יוסף: God's hand is stretched over us
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that even during הסתר פנים, God's hand stays stretched over us to protect us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: His hand is stretched out over us, as it says: 'And I have covered you in the shadow of My hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second explanation. During the hiding, God still protects us with His hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא pointed to dreams, a form of communication. רב יוסף points to protection. Both agree that הסתר פנים is not total abandonment.

keyTerms.meaning: His hand is stretched out over us
And I have covered you in the shadow of My hand

steps.whyThisMatters: This phrase, 'His hand is stretched out over us', is exactly what רבי יהושע signals in the next story.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
His hand is stretched out over us,
as it says: 'And I have covered you in the shadow of My hand.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:16

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר יָדוֹ נְטוּיָה עָלֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation next to רבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even during הסתר פנים, God's protecting hand is over us.

steps.title: The silent hand-sign debate in Caesar's house
steps.stepSummary: In the Caesar's palace, a מין signals to רבי יהושע בן חנניה that God turned His face from the Jews, and רבי יהושע signals back that God's hand is stretched over us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן חנניה was standing in the house of the Caesar. A certain heretic signaled to him: A nation whose Master turned His face away from it. He signaled back to him: His hand is stretched out over us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב יוסף's idea in action. A heretic mocks the Jews with a hand sign, and רבי יהושע answers with a hand sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretic uses הסתר פנים as proof that God abandoned the Jews. רבי יהושע answers with רב יוסף's teaching that God still protects them.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה הֲוָה קָאֵי בֵּי קֵיסָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya was standing in the house of the Caesar.
A certain heretic signaled to him:
A nation whose Master turned His face away from it.
He signaled to him: His hand is stretched out over us.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה הֲוָה קָאֵי בֵּי קֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing רב יוסף's idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע answers the heretic's sign with 'His hand is stretched out over us'.

steps.title: Caesar asks רבי יהושע to explain the signs
steps.stepSummary: The Caesar asks רבי יהושע what the signs meant, and he explains both sides of the exchange.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Caesar said to רבי יהושע: What did he signal to you? 'A nation whose Master turned His face away from it,' and I signaled to him, 'His hand is stretched out over us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The Caesar wants to know what the silent exchange meant. רבי יהושע explains exactly what the heretic said and what he answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע fully understands both signs, his own and the heretic's. That sets up the contrast in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he signal to you?

phrases.english: The Caesar said to Rabbi Yehoshua:
What did he signal to you?
'A nation whose Master turned His face away from it,'
phrases.notes: Now רבי יהושע is answering the Caesar.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנָא מַחְוֵינָא לֵיהּ יָדוֹ נְטוּיָה עָלֵינוּ.
phrases.english: and I signaled to him, 'His hand is stretched out over us.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מַאי אַחְוִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע explains both signs correctly.

steps.title: The heretic cannot explain רבי יהושע's sign
steps.stepSummary: The Caesar's people ask the heretic about the signs. He explains his own sign but admits he doesn't know what רבי יהושע signaled.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to that heretic: What did you signal to him? 'A nation whose Master turned away from it.' And what did he signal to you? I don't know.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the heretic is questioned. He can explain his own sign but not רבי יהושע's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of רבי יהושע, who understood everything. The heretic started the exchange but could not follow the reply.

phrases.english: They said to that heretic:
What did you signal to him?
'A nation whose Master turned away from it.'
And what did he signal to you?
I don't know.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְהָהוּא מִינָא מַאי אַחְוִיית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the other side of the exchange.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the heretic and רבי יהושע signaled.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heretic knows only his own sign.

steps.title: The heretic is executed
steps.stepSummary: The Caesar's people say a man who can't understand signs has no business signaling before the king, and they kill him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: A man who does not know what is signaled to him should signal with gestures before the king?! They took him out and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The heretic is judged unfit for signaling games in front of the king, and he is executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretic claimed God had abandoned the Jews, yet he himself is the one who ends up destroyed. The story closes by backing רב יוסף's idea that God's protecting hand is still over us.

keyTerms.meaning: They took him out and killed him

steps.whatToRemember: Even in a time of הסתר פנים, God has not abandoned us: He speaks in dreams (רבא) and His hand protects us (רב יוסף), as the story of רבי יהושע בן חנניה shows.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ: גַּבְרָא דְּלָא יָדַע מַאי מַחְווּ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: They said: A man who does not know what is signaled to him,
should signal with gestures before the king?!
They took him out and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ גַּבְרָא דְּלָא יָדַע מַאי מַחְווּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The heretic who mocked the Jews is killed, supporting the idea that God's hand still protects them.

steps.title: The Sages worry as רבי יהושע בן חנניה is dying
steps.stepSummary: As רבי יהושע בן חנניה is dying, the רבנן ask him what will happen to them with the מינים once he is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יהושע בן חנניה was dying, the רבנן said to him: What will become of us because of the heretics?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new part of the story of רבי יהושע בן חנניה. As he is dying, the רבנן ask a worried question, and his answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that רבי יהושע was the one who could out-argue the מינים, even in the Caesar's palace. Now the רבנן fear that without him, nobody will be able to answer the heretics.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul was resting, a gentle way of saying he was dying

phrases.english: When his soul was coming to rest
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya,
the Sages said to him:
What will become of us because of the heretics?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא נִיחָא נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories about רבי יהושע בן חנניה and the מינים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who will protect the Jewish people from the heretics once רבי יהושע is gone?

steps.title: When Israel loses wisdom, the nations lose theirs too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with a פסוק: when wisdom is lost from Israel, the wisdom of the nations is lost at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Counsel has perished from the children, their wisdom has spoiled.' Once counsel is lost from the children (Israel), the wisdom of the nations of the world spoils too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע calms the רבנן by quoting a פסוק and explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'children' as the Jewish people and 'their wisdom' as the wisdom of the nations. So the nations will never be smarter than Israel. When Israel's wisdom goes down, theirs goes down with it, and the balance stays the same.
steps.whatToRemember: The nations' wisdom rises and falls together with Israel's, so the heretics will never have the upper hand.

phrases.english: He said to them:
"Counsel has perished from the children,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 49:7

phrases.english: their wisdom has spoiled."
Once counsel has perished from the children,
phrases.notes: He reads 'the children' as the Jewish people.

phrases.english: the wisdom of the nations of the world has spoiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Sages' worried question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No need to fear. The nations' wisdom declines together with Israel's, so they will never be ahead.

steps.title: A second פסוק for the same idea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different פסוק to show that the nations move side by side with Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it from here: 'And he said: Let us travel and go, and I will go alongside you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another source for the same idea from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'I will go alongside you' show the nations moving exactly together with Israel. When Israel goes up they go up, and when Israel goes down they go down. So they never get ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another option)

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
"And he said: Let us travel and let us go,
phrases.notes: בראשית 33:12

phrases.english: and I will go alongside you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative פסוק for the idea in step 13
steps.raayaObject: The nations rise and fall together with Israel

steps.title: רבי אילא is frightened by a פסוק a child was reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא hears a child read that God tells a person 'what his speech was', and he cries out that such a servant has no hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא was going up the stairs of the house of רבה בר שילא. He heard a child reading: 'For behold, He forms mountains and creates wind, and tells a man what his speech was.' He said: A servant whose master tells him what his speech was, does he have any hope?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story. רבי אילא hears a פסוק and is shaken by it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God will show a person everything he said. רבי אילא realizes that if every word is reviewed, nobody can come out clean. This sets up the question in the next step about what 'his speech' includes.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy, hope of being fixed

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila was going up
the stairs of the house of Rabba bar Sheila.
He heard a child
who was reading:
"For behold, He forms mountains
phrases.notes: עמוס 4:13

phrases.english: and creates wind
and tells a man what his speech was."
He said:

phrases.aramaic: עֶבֶד שֶׁרַבּוֹ מַגִּיד לוֹ מַה שִּׂיחוֹ
phrases.english: A servant whose master tells him what his speech was,
does he have any hope?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִילָא הֲוָה סָלֵיק בְּדַרְגָּא דְּבֵי רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the fear of judgment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If God reviews all of a person's speech with him, there seems to be no hope for anyone.

steps.title: What does 'what his speech was' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of speech the פסוק is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'what his speech was'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the words in the פסוק. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could just mean sinful speech. The גמרא wants to know how far it really goes, which explains why רבי אילא was so scared.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "what his speech was"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What speech is included in 'what his speech was'?

steps.title: Even light talk between husband and wife is shown at death
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that even extra, light talk between a man and his wife is shown to a person when he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Even extra talk between a man and his wife is told to a person at the time of his death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question and explains how much the פסוק includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not only sinful words. Even small, private, unneeded talk between husband and wife is reviewed. That is why רבי אילא felt there was no hope.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Even extra talk
that is between a man and his wife
is told to a person at the time of death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even light talk between husband and wife is reviewed at death.

steps.title: But רב himself joked with his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: a story shows רב himself chatting and laughing with his wife, so how can such talk be a problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב כהנא was lying under רב's bed, and heard him chatting, laughing and doing his needs. He said: רב's mouth is like someone who never tasted a cooked dish. רב said to him: כהנא, get out! This is not proper conduct!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's statement with a story about רב himself. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said light talk between husband and wife is reviewed at death, which sounds like it is wrong. But רב himself chatted and laughed with his wife before being with her. So how could he call such talk something a person is judged for?

keyTerms.meaning: Did his needs, a polite way of saying marital relations

steps.confusionAlert: רב sends רב כהנא out because hiding under his bed is improper. The challenge is not about רב כהנא; it is about רב's own light talk with his wife.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rav Kahana
was lying under Rav's bed,
and he heard him chatting and laughing
and doing his needs.
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of saying he was with his wife.

phrases.english: He said:
Rav's mouth is like
someone who never tasted a cooked dish.
He said to him: Kahana, get out!
This is not proper conduct!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב כָּהֲנָא הֲוָה גָּנֵי תּוּתֵי פּוּרְיֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that light talk between husband and wife is reviewed at death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself chatted and laughed with his wife, so such talk cannot be something wrong.

steps.title: Light talk is allowed when needed to make peace with one's wife
steps.stepSummary: The two cases are different: רב's laughing was needed to make peace with his wife, while the forbidden talk is when that is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem: in the case where he needs to make peace with her, it is allowed. In the case where he does not need to, it is the talk that is shown to him at death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 18. It explains why רב could laugh with his wife even though he warned about light talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that רב's own behavior seemed to go against his teaching. The answer splits the cases. When light talk is needed to calm or win over one's wife, it is proper. Extra light talk with no such need is what a person is shown after he dies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
To appease her, to make peace with her and win her over

steps.whatToRemember: Talk between husband and wife is judged by its purpose. Words that build closeness and peace are proper. Empty, extra light talk is what gets counted.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where he needs to appease her,
phrases.notes: This is the story of רב laughing with his wife. There, the talk was needed.

phrases.english: this, where he does not need to appease her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's own laughing with his wife seems to show that light talk is no problem
steps.terutzMaskana: Light talk that is needed to make peace with one's wife is allowed. Talk without that need is what a person is shown at death.

steps.title: God has a hidden place called מסתרים where He cries
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אינייא in the name of רב reads 'במסתרים' as the name of a hidden place where God cries.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'If you will not listen, my soul will cry in secret places because of pride.' רב שמואל בר אינייא said in the name of רב: הקדוש ברוך הוא has a place, and its name is 'מסתרים' (Hidden Places).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching on a פסוק in ירמיהו. It explains that 'במסתרים' is the name of a special place where God cries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading could just be 'secretly.' רב reads it as a real place belonging to הקדוש ברוך הוא, set aside for His crying. This idea of a hidden place will matter later, when the גמרא asks how God can cry at all.

phrases.english: "But if you will not hear it,
my soul shall weep in secret places
because of pride."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 13:17

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Inya said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has a place
and its name is Mistarim.
phrases.notes: He reads the word as the name of a place, not just as 'secretly.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לֹא תִשְׁמָעוּהָ בְּמִסְתָּרִים תִּבְכֶּה נַפְשִׁי מִפְּנֵי גֵוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new אגדה teaching, moving on from the topic of judgment at death
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא has a hidden place called מסתרים where He cries

steps.title: What pride is God crying about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'מפני גוה' means: whose pride is God crying over?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'because of pride' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the last words of the פסוק. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know where God cries, but not over what. 'Pride' is unclear. It could be the pride of Israel or some other pride, so the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: What is; what does it mean

phrases.english: What is "because of pride"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the end of the פסוק quoted in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose pride the פסוק means when it says God cries 'because of pride'

steps.title: The pride of Israel that was given to the nations
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק says God cries over Israel's pride, which was taken away and given to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: God cries because of the pride of Israel, which was taken from them and given to the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question 'what pride?' God cries because Israel lost its honor and the nations received it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'גוה' means Israel's greatness and honor. God cries over the fall of His people from their place of honor.

keyTerms.meaning: The pride, the greatness, of Israel

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
because of the pride of Israel,
which was taken from them and given to the nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: מִפְּנֵי גַּאֲווֹתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God cries over Israel's pride, which was taken from them and given to the nations

steps.title: The pride of the kingdom of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says God cries over the pride of מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: God cries because of the pride of the kingdom of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to 'what pride?' God cries over the honor of His own kingship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer was about Israel's honor. This answer is about God's honor: His kingship is less seen in the world, and that is what He cries over.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingdom of Heaven, God's rule in the world

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
because of the pride of the kingdom of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי גַּאֲווֹתָהּ שֶׁל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God cries over the lost honor of His own kingship

steps.title: How can there be crying before God if there is no sadness before Him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of God crying, using רב פפא's teaching that there is no sadness before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there crying before הקדוש ברוך הוא? Didn't רב פפא say: There is no sadness before הקדוש ברוך הוא, as the פסוק says, 'Glory and beauty are before Him, strength and joy are in His place'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the teaching of step 20. It brings a statement and a פסוק showing that only joy is found before God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said God cries in a place called מסתרים. רב פפא, based on a פסוק, says there is only joy and strength 'in His place.' These two ideas seem to clash.

phrases.english: But is there crying
before the Holy One, Blessed be He?
But didn't Rav Pappa say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עֲצִיבוּת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: There is no sadness before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is stated: "Honor and majesty are before Him;
strength and gladness are in His place"!
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 16:27

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא בְּכִיָּה קַמֵּיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא? וְהָאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 20 that God cries
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that God cries in a place called מסתרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says only strength and joy are in God's place, so there should be no crying before Him

steps.title: Crying in the inner rooms, joy in the outer rooms
steps.stepSummary: God cries only in the hidden inner rooms; in the outer rooms there is only joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem: this one (crying) is in the inner rooms, and that one (no sadness) is in the outer rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting between two kinds of 'places.' God's crying is hidden inside; outside there is only joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the word 'מסתרים', meaning hidden places. The crying is real but kept inside. The 'joy in His place' of רב פפא's פסוק refers to the outer rooms.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is in the inner rooms,
phrases.notes: The crying of step 20 happens here, in the hidden place.

phrases.english: that is in the outer rooms.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּבָתֵּי גַוָּאֵי, הָא בְּבָתֵּי בַרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There can be no crying at all before God
steps.terutzMaskana: Crying happens only in the inner, hidden rooms; the outer rooms have only joy

steps.title: A פסוק shows God calling for crying openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there is really no crying in the outer rooms, since a פסוק shows God calling openly for weeping and mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the outer rooms is there no crying? But it is written: 'And on that day the Lord, God of hosts, called for crying and mourning, for tearing out hair and wearing sackcloth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 25. It brings a פסוק where God's mourning seems open, not hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the outer rooms have only joy. But in ישעיהו, God openly calls for weeping and signs of mourning. That looks like sadness in the outer rooms too.

keyTerms.meaning: Baldness, from tearing out hair in mourning

phrases.english: And in the outer rooms, not?
But isn't it written: "And the Lord, God of hosts, called
on that day for weeping and for mourning,
and for baldness and for girding with sackcloth"!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there is no sadness in the outer rooms
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows God calling openly for weeping and mourning, which means sadness is not only hidden

steps.title: The destruction of the בית המקדש is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The חורבן of the בית המקדש is different: then even the angels of peace cried openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The destruction of the בית המקדש is different, for even the angels of peace cried, as it says: 'Behold, their mighty ones cried outside; the angels of peace weep bitterly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 26. The open mourning in that פסוק was for the חורבן, which is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule stays: God's crying is hidden in the inner rooms. The חורבן was so terrible that the sadness broke out into the open, and even the angels of peace cried 'outside.'

keyTerms.meaning: The destruction of the Holy Temple

steps.whatToRemember: God's crying is normally hidden in the inner rooms. The חורבן of the בית המקדש is the one exception, where even the angels cried openly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how great the loss of the בית המקדש is: it is the one sorrow that is not kept hidden even above.

phrases.english: The destruction of the Temple is different,
for even the angels of peace cried,
as it is stated: "Behold, their valiant ones cry outside;
phrases.notes: 'Outside' fits the outer rooms. The crying was out in the open.

phrases.english: the angels of peace weep bitterly."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in ישעיהו shows open sadness, against the rule of step 25
steps.terutzMaskana: Normally there is no sadness in the outer rooms, but the חורבן was so great that even angels cried openly

steps.title: Three tear-words in the verse mean three tragedies
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the three tear-words in the פסוק stand for the first מקדש, the second מקדש, and the exile of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "My eye will weep and weep and run down with tears, because God's flock is taken captive." רבי אלעזר asked: why three tear-words? One is for the first בית המקדש, one is for the second בית המקדש, and one is for ישראל who were exiled from their land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rest of the פסוק it has been discussing. רבי אלעזר explains why it uses three separate words for tears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says דָּמֹעַ, תִּדְמַע and דִּמְעָה, which looks like extra wording. רבי אלעזר reads each word as crying over a different disaster. The third disaster, the exile, matches the end of the פסוק: 'God's flock is taken captive.'

keyTerms.meaning: God's flock, meaning the Jewish people

phrases.english: "And my eye shall weep and weep, and run down with tears,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 13:17. Count the tear-words: דָּמֹעַ, תִּדְמַע, דִּמְעָה. That makes three.

phrases.english: because God's flock is carried away captive."
Rabbi Elazar said:
Why are there these three tears?
One is for the First Temple,
and one is for the Second Temple,
and one is for the Jewish people, who were exiled from their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק about God's crying and explains its repeated tear-words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three tears stand for the first מקדש, the second מקדש, and the exile of ישראל.

steps.title: Another view: the third tear is for ביטול תורה
steps.stepSummary: Another opinion says the third tear is for the stopping of Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the third tear is for ביטול תורה, when Torah learning stops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion about what the third tear stands for. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two tears stay the same: the two בתי מקדש. Only the third tear changes. Instead of the exile itself, this opinion says it is for the loss of Torah learning.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version or opinion)
The stopping or neglect of Torah learning

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
One is for the stopping of Torah learning.
phrases.notes: This replaces only the third tear. The two tears for the בתי מקדש stay the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation for the third tear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third tear is for ביטול תורה.

steps.title: How does ביטול תורה fit the end of the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ביטול תורה opinion explains the words 'God's flock is taken captive.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says the third tear is for the exile, because the פסוק says 'God's flock is taken captive.' But for the one who says it is for ביטול תורה, what do the words 'God's flock is taken captive' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second opinion. The end of the פסוק talks about captivity, not about Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'God's flock is taken captive' fits the exile opinion perfectly. For the ביטול תורה opinion, that phrase seems to have nothing to do with the tear. So the second opinion looks like it does not match the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one side)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said
that it is for the Jewish people who were exiled,
that is why it is written:
"because God's flock is carried away captive."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַל בִּיטּוּל תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: But according to the one who said it is for the stopping of Torah learning,
what is the meaning of "because God's flock is carried away captive"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the third tear is for ביטול תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the פסוק speaks about captivity, which fits only the exile opinion.

steps.title: Exile is the greatest ביטול תורה
steps.stepSummary: Once ישראל were exiled, Torah learning was lost more than at any other time, so the end of the פסוק fits this opinion too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since ישראל were exiled from their land, there is no greater ביטול תורה than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The captivity in the פסוק is the cause of the ביטול תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק is not about something separate. It gives the reason for the third tear: the exile brought about the worst loss of Torah learning. So both opinions can read the end of the פסוק the same way.

phrases.english: Since the Jewish people were exiled from their place,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ בִּיטּוּל תּוֹרָה גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: there is no greater stopping of Torah learning than this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the captivity is the cause of the ביטול תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words about captivity fit only the exile opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exile caused the greatest ביטול תורה, so the פסוק fits both opinions.

steps.title: Three things God cries over every day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three people הקדוש ברוך הוא cries over every day: one who can learn but does not, one who can hardly learn but does, and a proud leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: הקדוש ברוך הוא cries over three people every day. He cries over someone who can learn Torah and does not. He cries over someone who can hardly learn Torah and learns anyway. And He cries over a community leader who acts proudly over the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that keeps going with the theme of God crying. This time it lists three people He cries over every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two cases are opposites. One person has the chance to learn and wastes it. The other has almost no chance and learns anyway. The third case, a proud leader, connects back to the earlier theme of pride (step 23).

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
To be busy with Torah learning
Who acts proudly, lords over others

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹכֶה עֲלֵיהֶן בְּכׇל יוֹם:
phrases.english: There are three that the Holy One, Blessed be He, cries over every day:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ עוֹסֵק,
phrases.english: over one who is able to learn Torah and does not learn,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲסוֹק בְּתוֹרָה וְעוֹסֵק,
phrases.english: and over one who is unable to learn Torah and learns anyway,
and over a leader who acts proudly over the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching on the theme of God's crying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God cries daily over one who can learn and does not, one who cannot easily learn yet does, and a proud leader.

steps.title: רבי drops the book of איכה
steps.stepSummary: While reading איכה, רבי reached the פסוק about being thrown from heaven to earth, and the book fell from his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי was holding the book of איכה and reading it. When he reached the פסוק "He threw down from heaven to earth," the book fell from his hand. He said: "From a high roof to a deep pit!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows how deeply רבי felt the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes ישראל falling from the highest place to the lowest. רבי was so shaken that the book dropped from his hand. His saying puts the fall into a picture: not a small drop, but from a high roof all the way into a deep pit.
steps.whatToRemember: Crying runs through this whole section: God crying in מסתרים, the three tears in ירמיהו for the חורבן and the exile, God's daily crying, and רבי dropping the book of איכה from grief.

phrases.english: Rabbi was holding the book of Lamentations
phrases.notes: When the גמרא just says 'רבי', it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and was reading in it.
When he reached this verse:
"He has thrown down from heaven to earth,"
phrases.notes: איכה 2:1

phrases.english: it fell from his hand.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the book of איכה he was holding.

phrases.english: He said: From a high roof to a deep pit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that carries on the theme of grief over the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fall of ישראל was from the greatest height to the lowest depth.

steps.title: רבי and רבי חייא want to greet a blind scholar
steps.stepSummary: While traveling, רבי and רבי חייא look for a local scholar to greet. They find out he is blind, and רבי חייא tells רבי to stay behind so he does not lower his honor as נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי and רבי חייא were walking on the road. When they reached a certain town, they asked: Is there a Torah scholar here we can go and greet? The people said: There is a Torah scholar here, but he is blind. רבי חייא said to רבי: You stay here. Do not lower the honor of your position as נשיא. I will go and greet him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story. It sets the scene: two great sages want to greet a local scholar, and רבי חייא suggests that רבי stay behind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's concern is about honor. A נשיא going out of his way to visit a lesser scholar might look like it lowers the dignity of his office. The scholar's blindness will become the key to the blessing in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A young or local Torah scholar
Let us greet him (literally, receive his face)
A polite way of saying 'blind' (literally, 'light of eyes')
The position of נשיא, the leader of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: מאור עינים sounds like it means 'sharp-sighted', but here it is a polite way of saying the man is blind.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲווֹ שָׁקְלִי וְאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi and Rabbi Chiya were walking along the road.
When they arrived at a certain town,
they said: Is there a Torah scholar here?
Let us go and greet him.
They said: There is a Torah scholar here,
phrases.notes: This time it is the people of the town answering.

phrases.english: but he is blind.
Rabbi Chiya said to Rabbi:
You sit here. Do not lower the honor of your position as Nasi.
I will go and greet him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲווֹ שָׁקְלִי וְאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new אגדה story after the story of רבי reading איכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבי חייא advises רבי not to lower the honor of the נשיא by visiting a blind scholar.

steps.title: The blind scholar blesses them
steps.stepSummary: רבי insists on going along. When they leave, the blind scholar blesses them to merit greeting the One Who sees but is not seen. רבי tells רבי חייא he would have missed this blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי grabbed him and went with him. When they were leaving, the scholar said to them: You greeted a face that is seen but does not see. May you merit to greet the Face that sees but is not seen. רבי said to רבי חייא: If I had listened to you just now, you would have kept me from this blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ignores the advice and goes along to greet the scholar. They receive a special blessing, and רבי points out what he would have lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing turns the blindness around. The scholar can be seen but cannot see, while הקדוש ברוך הוא sees everything but cannot be seen. רבי's remark shows that humbly honoring a scholar was worth more than protecting the honor of his office.

keyTerms.meaning: He grabbed him / insisted on him
The One Who sees but is not seen, meaning הקדוש ברוך הוא

phrases.english: He grabbed him and went with him.
phrases.notes: It is רבי who insists on coming along with רבי חייא.

phrases.english: When they were leaving him,
he said to them: You greeted a face
that is seen but does not see,
may you merit to greet the Face
that sees but is not seen.
phrases.notes: He means הקדוש ברוך הוא.

phrases.english: He said to him: If just now
you would have kept me from this blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: רבי goes despite רבי חייא's advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greeting a scholar earns a blessing to greet the שכינה; honoring a scholar outweighs protecting one's own honor.

steps.title: Where did you learn this blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The two sages ask the blind scholar where he learned that greeting scholars deserves such a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: From whom did you hear this?
steps.whatsHappening: The sages ask the blind scholar for the source of his idea. This sets up his explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are not asking about the wording of the blessing. They want to know where he learned that greeting a scholar is great enough to deserve such a reward.

phrases.english: They said to him: From whom did you hear this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the blessing given in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the idea that greeting Torah scholars brings such a great reward.

steps.title: רבי יעקב kept greeting his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The blind scholar says he learned it from רבי יעקב, who greeted his teacher every day. When רבי יעקב grew old, his teacher told him he no longer needed to trouble himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: I heard it from the teaching of רבי יעקב. רבי יעקב of the village of חיטייא used to greet his teacher every day. When he grew old, his teacher said to him: Let the master not trouble himself, since the master is no longer able.
steps.whatsHappening: The blind scholar starts to answer by telling an earlier story about רבי יעקב and his teacher. The teacher's suggestion sets up רבי יעקב's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher was being kind, excusing his elderly student from a hard daily visit. This shows how seriously רבי יעקב took greeting his teacher, and it prepares for his explanation of why he would not stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a respectful way of saying 'you'

phrases.english: I heard it from the teaching of Rabbi Yaakov,
for Rabbi Yaakov of the village of Chitiya

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְקַבֵּיל אַפֵּיהּ דְּרַבֵּיהּ כׇּל יוֹמָא.
phrases.english: used to greet his teacher every day.
When he grew old, he said to him:
phrases.notes: Here the teacher is speaking to רבי יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: לָא נִצְטַעַר מָר, דְּלָא יָכֵיל מָר.
phrases.english: Let the master not trouble himself, since the master is not able.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 36 by naming the source, רבי יעקב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learned it from רבי יעקב, who greeted his teacher daily even into old age.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a פסוק in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב answers his teacher with a פסוק: one who sees sages die will live. A קל וחומר follows: seeing them while they are alive is surely even greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to him: Is it a small thing, what is written about the sages: 'That he should still live forever, that he should not see the pit, for he sees that wise men die'? If one who sees sages at their death will live, then one who sees them in their lifetime, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב explains why he will not stop greeting his teacher. He brings a פסוק and builds a קל וחומר from it. This completes the blind scholar's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links life to seeing wise men at their death. From that, רבי יעקב reasons that seeing them while they are alive must bring an even greater reward. This is why the blind scholar knew that greeting רבי and רבי חייא deserved a blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: A reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: Greeting Torah scholars is a great merit. If even seeing them at their death brings life, then seeing them while they are alive is surely greater. That is why the blind scholar blessed רבי and רבי חייא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the source of the blessing in step 35 and teaches the importance of visiting and greeting תלמידי חכמים.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it a small thing,
phrases.notes: Now רבי יעקב is answering his teacher.

phrases.english: what is written about the sages:
'That he should still live forever, that he should not see the pit,'
'for he sees that wise men die.'
Now, if one who sees sages at their death will live,
then one who sees them in their lifetime, all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, מִי זוּטַר מַאי דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ בְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יעקב replies to his teacher's suggestion with a source, which finishes the answer to step 36.
steps.raayaObject: That greeting Torah scholars is a great merit worthy of reward.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 49:10–11, through a קל וחומר from seeing sages at their death to seeing them in their lifetime.

steps.title: רב אידי is mocked as a one-day student
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי traveled three months to spend one day in the yeshiva. The רבנן called him a one-day student, and he was hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי, the father of רבי יעקב בר אידי, used to travel three months on the road and spend one day in the yeshiva. The רבנן called him 'the one-day student.' He was hurt and applied to himself the פסוק: 'I am a laughingstock to my friend.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a man who worked very hard to learn Torah for only one day, and was mocked for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי's effort was huge: three months of travel for one day of learning. The רבנן only saw the short time in the yeshiva, not the effort behind it. His quoting of the פסוק shows how deeply the teasing hurt him.

keyTerms.meaning: The yeshiva, the house of study
A student for one day, a mocking nickname
He read a פסוק as being about himself

phrases.aramaic: רַב אִידִי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
phrases.english: Rav Idi, the father of Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi,
was used to traveling
three months on the road
and spending one day in the yeshiva,
and the Sages would call him
'the one-day student.'
He felt hurt,
and read about himself:
'I am a laughingstock to my friend, etc.'
phrases.notes: איוב 12:4.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אִידִי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי הֲוָה רְגִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about the value of time spent with Torah and scholars, following the story of the blind scholar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אידי was mocked for learning only one day, despite his great effort, and he was deeply hurt.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks רב אידי not to punish the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begs רב אידי not to let his hurt bring punishment on the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Please, I beg you, do not punish the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן steps in and asks רב אידי to hold back his hurt feelings so the רבנן won't be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that רבי יוחנן worries about this shows that the pain of a hurt Torah scholar is taken very seriously. רבי יוחנן does not deny that רב אידי was wronged; he asks him to be forgiving.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
Please, I beg of you,
do not punish the Sages.
phrases.notes: He means: don't let your hurt feelings cause the Sages to be punished from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּמָטוּתָא מִינָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב אידי's hurt from step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן asks רב אידי not to bring punishment on the רבנן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן quotes a verse about seeking God daily
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן goes to the בית מדרש and teaches the פסוק 'And Me they seek day by day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן went out to the בית מדרש and taught: 'And Me they seek day by day, and they desire to know My ways.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן goes public to defend רב אידי. Here he only quotes the פסוק, setting up a question about its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'יום יום' (day by day) will be the key. The next step will ask why the פסוק mentions only day.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught a lesson from a פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan went out to the study hall
and taught:
'And Me they seek day by day,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:2.

phrases.english: and they desire to know My ways.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן moves from a private request to a public teaching that defends רב אידי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'ואותי יום יום ידרשון' is brought as the basis for a lesson.

steps.title: Do people seek God only by day?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks: does the פסוק mean God is sought by day but not at night?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really that they seek Him by day and not at night?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן points out a strange detail in the פסוק: it says 'day' and not night. This question sets up his real lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Obviously people seek ה׳ at night too, so the word 'day' must be teaching something else. The question pushes us to read 'יום' in a new way.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so? (a question showing surprise)

phrases.english: Is it really that by day they seek Him
and at night they do not seek Him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק speak only of 'day' when God is sought at night too?

steps.title: One day of Torah counts like a whole year
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that learning Torah even one day a year is counted as if one learned all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to tell you: anyone who learns Torah even one day a year, the פסוק counts it for him as if he learned the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers his question: 'יום' means one single day, and that one day is counted as a whole year of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'יום יום' is read as one day standing for a full year. This directly defends רב אידי, who learned one day a year. His 'one day' is not something to mock, because ה׳ counts it as a full year.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you
The פסוק counts it for him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of רבי יוחנן's defense of רב אידי: the effort of one day of Torah is counted fully.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:
anyone who learns Torah
even one day a year —
the verse counts it for him
as if he learned the entire year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לָךְ: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Day' teaches that one day of Torah a year is counted as a full year of learning.

steps.title: The same rule for punishment: the spies
steps.stepSummary: The same idea applies to punishment, as shown by the פסוק about the spies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true for punishment, as it is written: 'According to the number of days that you scouted the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says the same rule works in the opposite direction, for sin. He quotes the פסוק about the spies to set up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spies scouted for forty days, and בני ישראל were punished with forty years. This sets up the question that comes next.

phrases.english: And the same is true for punishment,
as it is written:
'According to the number of days
that you scouted the land.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:34. The פסוק goes on: forty days, a year for each day, you will bear your sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 43 from reward to punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same day-for-year rule applies to punishment.

steps.title: Did they sin for forty years?
steps.stepSummary: The question: they were punished forty years, but they only sinned for forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they sin for forty years? They only sinned for forty days!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן points out a puzzle: the punishment lasted forty years, but the sin lasted only forty days. This sets up the lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gap between forty days and forty years needs explaining. The answer will use the same idea as before: one day counts as a year.

phrases.english: Did they sin for forty years?
But they sinned only for forty days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the פסוק quoted in step 44.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why were they punished forty years for a forty-day sin?

steps.title: One day of sin counts like a whole year
steps.stepSummary: Sinning even one day a year is counted as if one sinned the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to tell you: anyone who does a sin even one day a year, the פסוק counts it against him as if he sinned the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: each day of the spies' sin counted as a full year, so forty days became forty years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 43 exactly, but for sin instead of Torah. Together the two show that one day can count as a whole year, both for good and for bad.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן teaches that one day a year can count as a full year: for Torah learning (reward) and for sin (punishment). This defends רב אידי's one day in the yeshiva.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:
anyone who does a sin
even one day a year —
the verse counts it against him
as if he sinned the entire year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לָךְ: כׇּל הָעוֹבֵר עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 45, paralleling step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One day of sin a year is counted as a full year, so forty days of sin became forty years of punishment.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: who is a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: a קטן is any child who cannot ride on his father's shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is a קטן? Any child who cannot ride on his father's shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the stories and goes back to the משנה, quoting its definition of a קטן who is exempt from coming to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures a child's obligation by whether he can ride on his father's shoulders up to the Temple Mount. This quote sets up a challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: Who is a minor —
anyone who is not able
to ride on his father's shoulders.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה, about which child is exempt from coming up to the בית המקדש on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to the משנה's list of who is exempt from coming to the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן is a child who cannot ride on his father's shoulders.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins an objection
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא begins a challenge to the משנה's definition of a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged this:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens a challenge. רבי זירא is about to attack the משנה's definition, and the content of his question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מתקיף לה' means a strong objection. The target is the shoulder-riding test of step 47.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who raises the challenge

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly challenged this:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the definition quoted in step 47.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's definition of a קטן as one who cannot ride on his father's shoulders.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The details of the attack come next; here רבי זירא only signals that he finds the definition hard.
